feedback: Approving this candidate for the race. Iteration 0 was 0 finishes in 60 trials, with every run ending off_track and max_error of about 0.06 m on all three tracks (iteration 0 outcome table). That makes overshoot on bends the failure to test, so this candidate changes the control aggressiveness rather than the sensing. Two corrections to the rationale. First, the off-track limit is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4). With body_width 0.18 the second term is 0.0575 m, so the 0.06 m floor still applies and the wider body adds no margin. Second, base_speed 1.3 gives base PWM of about 2660, which is below the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s. Finishing will likely need base_speed back toward 1.5 to 1.6 once the robot stays on the line. The other changes (kp 2.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, sensors at y 0.06) are sensible and in range. Next race: if the robot stays on track and progress rises well above 0.04, use the telemetry to set speed. If it still goes off_track with max_error above 0.06 m, lower kp further. If it completes but takes over 3 s, raise base_speed.
requested_changes: If the race completes but completion_time is above 3 s: raise base_speed from 1.3 to about 1.5 to 1.6, keeping kp 2.5 and kd 0.8, since iteration 0 showed the off-track failure is caused by aggressive steering rather than sensing.

If the race still ends off_track with max_error above 0.06 m (iteration 0 baseline 0.0608 on oval): lower kp from 2.5 to about 1.8 and keep base_speed 1.3, because steering overshoot is the suspected cause.
If steering_oscillation stays high (iteration 0 baseline 0.07 to 0.16) after the robot stays on track: raise kd from 0.8 to about 1.2 before changing kp.
